detail: US census adults (income, sex, race, age, hs_week); bambi logistic_regression-style example with no repeated cluster unit or random effect (brief list).
ANES 2016 pilot vote survey (vote, age, party_id); bambi logistic_regression example, fixed effects only, one row per respondent, no grouping factor (brief list).
Personality / drug-use scores (drugs, Big Five sub-scores); bambi ESCS_multiple_regression example, ordinary multiple regression with no random effect (brief list).
Car insurance claims (claim cost/number by vehicle and driver attributes); bambi regression example with no sampled clustering unit modelled as a random effect (brief list).
Kyoto cherry-blossom day-of-year and temperature by year (one row per year); bambi splines_cherry_blossoms example fits a spline of year, fixed effects only, no grouping factor (brief list).
Motor Trend cars (mpg and specs, one row per car); bambi regression example with no grouping factor (brief list).
Graduate admissions (admit, gre, gpa, rank); bambi alternative_links_binary example, binary GLM with no random effect; rank is the predictor of interest not a sampled cluster (brief list).
bambi circular_regression example fits direction ~ distance (von Mises); only two columns (distance, direction), 31 rows, no grouping factor.

Hourly Capital Bikeshare rental counts; bambi serves it via load_data but the current docs fit it no mixed model (the negative_binomial/spline examples use other data). A count GLM over time/weather covariates has no grouping factor; essentially one hourly time series.

MixedModels.jl benchmark-only dataset: three abstract crossed grouping factors g/h/i, covariate u, and a small signed-integer response y (negatives present), fit as y ~ 1 + u + (1|g) + (1|h) + (1|i) solely for performance benchmarking. No real-world provenance; synthetic/simulated per the brief, excluded.

Mirror of lme4 Dyestuff2, which the lme4 help page states is simulated (generated in the structure of Dyestuff to illustrate a zero among-batch variance). Excluded per the simulated-data rule, consistent with the lme4 re-filing (#20).
